_schema.purpose: Current ENSO state and the mechanisms by which it couples to this project's subject matter. Consumed by ENSO-coupling.py.
_schema.why_this_file_exists: This repo had no ENSO content of any kind before 2026-08-21. That is a gap, because a very strong El Nino modulates stratospheric transport, column ozone, and the logistics fragility this project treats as its outcome variable. It is also an attribution hazard: anything observed in the 2026-27 window has a large natural driver that must be removed before attributing it to satellite reentry.
_schema.reading_this_file: Every quantitative field carries a `status`. Nothing here is a coupling coefficient. ENSO-coupling.py will not multiply chi by anything from this file — see `coupling_status` on each mechanism, and RESEARCH_LOG.md U-21.

status_values.sourced: From a named external product. See `reference`.
status_values.mechanism_established: The physical mechanism is standard in the literature, but its magnitude for THIS aerosol population is not quantified here.
status_values.unquantified: Known or suspected to matter; no number in this repo.

_schema.verification_warning: Gathered by web search on 2026-08-21. NOAA CPC (cpc.ncep.noaa.gov), arxiv.org and other primary domains were blocked by this environment's network egress policy, so these figures come from SEARCH SUMMARIES of the CPC/IRI products, not from the products themselves. Every value is marked verified_against_primary: false. ENSO figures are updated monthly and go stale fast — re-check before use. Same caveat class as RESEARCH_LOG.md U-14.

oni_mjj_2026_c.note: ONI and the raw Nino-3.4 seasonal mean are different indices — ONI is a running mean referenced to centred 30-year base periods — so +1.39 and +1.51 for the same season are not necessarily in conflict. Recorded separately rather than reconciled.

historic_event_ond_2026_pct.definition: three-month RONI >= +2.5 C, which would exceed every El Nino in the record back to 1950

conflicting_figure_not_reconciled.claim: roughly 60% chance of reaching 'strong' (Nino-3.4 above +1.5 C)
conflicting_figure_not_reconciled.problem: Inconsistent with the >90% very-strong and 81% OND very-strong figures above — a very strong event is a subset of a strong one, so P(strong) cannot be below P(very strong). Most likely a stale forecast from an earlier issuance, or a garbled summary.
conflicting_figure_not_reconciled.resolution: NOT resolved. The internally consistent set (90 / 81 / 69) is used, and this figure is recorded so the discrepancy is visible rather than silently dropped. Check the primary product. See RESEARCH_LOG.md U-20.

coupling_mechanisms.name: Brewer-Dobson circulation / tropical upwelling modulation
coupling_mechanisms.description: El Nino is associated with enhanced tropical upwelling and a strengthened Brewer-Dobson circulation in the lower stratosphere, altering stratosphere-troposphere exchange and poleward transport.
coupling_mechanisms.why_it_matters_here: This modulates the residence time of stratospheric aerosol — the single most contested parameter in this repo (H-13, where two cited sources disagree by 6x). ENSO is a periodic modulator ON TOP of that already-unresolved baseline.
coupling_mechanisms.coupling_status: NOT WIRED IN. The model uses a single fixed residence time with no interannual variability of any kind.

coupling_mechanisms.name: ENSO-driven column ozone variability
coupling_mechanisms.description: ENSO drives substantial column ozone variability through transport, typically reducing tropical column ozone and redistributing it to mid-latitudes during El Nino.
coupling_mechanisms.why_it_matters_here: The repo's headline thresholds include a 220 DU ozone figure. ENSO-driven variability is a large confounder on any ozone trend, and a very strong event makes attribution of an ozone anomaly to Al2O3 catalysis substantially harder over the affected window.
coupling_mechanisms.coupling_status: NOT WIRED IN. No ozone model in this repo carries an ENSO term.

coupling_mechanisms.name: Drought / flood teleconnections to supply chain
coupling_mechanisms.description: El Nino drives well-documented regional drought and flood patterns affecting agriculture, inland waterways, and port operations.
coupling_mechanisms.why_it_matters_here: This is the repo's own outcome variable. The README's central 'Logistics-Fragility Feedback' claim is that PNT and grid disruption propagate into just-in-time supply chains. A historic El Nino is a live, independent stress test of that same supply chain — which makes it both an opportunity to calibrate the logistics model and a source of effects that could be misread as coupling-driven.
coupling_mechanisms.coupling_status: NOT WIRED IN. The logistics coupling is narrative only — no code implements it (it has never been implemented for any driver, ENSO or otherwise).

coupling_mechanisms.name: ENSO modulation of ionospheric variability
coupling_mechanisms.description: ENSO alters tropospheric wave forcing that propagates upward and can modulate ionospheric total electron content, which is the dominant error term in single-frequency GNSS positioning.
coupling_mechanisms.why_it_matters_here: The repo attributes PNT degradation to Al2O3-mediated EM coupling. ENSO offers a competing natural driver on the same observable.
coupling_mechanisms.coupling_status: NOT WIRED IN. Marked speculative — the mechanism chain is long and the repo has verified none of it.

coupling_mechanisms.name: Attribution hazard over the 2026-27 window
coupling_mechanisms.description: A record or near-record El Nino supplies a large natural forcing to every observable this project cares about: stratospheric transport, column ozone, PNT reliability, and supply-chain performance.
coupling_mechanisms.why_it_matters_here: This is the most immediately consequential item in this file, and it cuts AGAINST the project's thesis being credited for anything in 2026-27. See RESEARCH_LOG.md H-17 — the repo's own model predicts chi ~0.003 for that window, three orders of magnitude below its lowest risk regime, which means the model itself rules out satellite attribution for anything observed there.
coupling_mechanisms.coupling_status: Now documented. This is the one item here that required no new physics, only reading the model's own output.
